chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Les Hite band personnel
summary: Royal names Lloyd Reese, the saxophone section, Les Hite's accident, and Lionel Hampton as drummer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So when you came back and Hite's
Okay, joined Les Hight's band. Lawrence was in it. Who else was in it?
Well, I think I -- let's see, who --
We didn't go through that personnel,

There was a good trumpet player in that band by the name of Lloyd Reese (PHONETIC). Excellent. He became a teacher in this area here and he was excellent saxophonist, also an excellent trumpet player and excellent teacher. He went to school to Whittier College and he studied music out in that grouping out there. Then we had a very, very good saxophone section. We had a fellow by the name of Marvin Johnson (PHONETIC), played alto with me and Bumps Meyers (PHONETIC) was a tenor saxophone player. Then they had Charlie Jones (PHONETIC) was the other saxophone player and I and then Les Hight himself was a saxophone player. But he had the unfortunate happening of getting in an automobile accident and knocked his teeth formations out of place, so he didn't play any more after that. So we just played with the four.

Then Lawrence played -- Lionel Hampton was the drummer in the band and he worked there for many years with us. That's where I first got to be very good friends with Lionel Hampton. That's when he was deriving his style of playing two-finger piano and xylophones, vibraphones, actually, and then when Lionel formed his band in 1941, I formed his band, worked as his music director with him. I rehearsed his band, put it together for him, picked most of its men from this area out here. My brother, (ERNIE) was the lead trumpet player in the band at the time, and sent him out to make six million, for which I was never repaid in money very well. He was pretty cheap, although he was a nice man, I guess.
